# Flow export + DDoS + anomaly: current flow digest

<!-- LIVING digest: the current shape of this subsystem. Update it when you change the subsystem. -->
<!-- Generated by tracing the code; verify file:line before relying on a detail. -->
<!-- digest-base: internal/plugins/flowexport internal/plugins/trafficusage internal/plugins/ddos internal/plugins/anomaly -->

## What it is
Three independent plugin families share one capture/observation spine. `trafficusage` (eBPF TCX per-port/per-IP byte counters) and `flowexport` (sFlow/NetFlow v9/IPFIX counter export + conntrack flow records) both ride the interface rate-tracker's ~1 Hz callback and both tap the same process-wide `observation.Feed` with per-source-IP and per-flow facts. Two neutral aggregators consume that feed independently: `trafficstat` (per-interface/talker rates, feeds `ddos-detect`) and `trafficfeature` (per-source behavioral facts, fan-out, out/in ratio, port-entropy, new-peer, rare-port, beaconing, feeds `anomaly-detect`). On top, `ddos/detect` applies volumetric-DDoS judgment (rate threshold → fast target → flow-based family/vector characterization) and `anomaly/detect` applies behavioral judgment (per-entity EWMA baseline → z-score/cohort-rarity scoring), each emitting its own typed event contract (`ddosevent`, `anomalyevent`) that independent responders subscribe to: `ddos/local` (on-host nft drop), `ddos/flowspec` (upstream BGP FlowSpec, largely stubbed today, see gotchas), `ddos/observe`+`ddos/flowtriq` (incident ring + cloud reporting), and `anomaly/shape` (shadow-first per-source firewall arm with auto-revert/kill-switch). Every plugin here runs as an internal (in-process) goroutine; all inter-plugin data flow is either the typed `ze.EventBus` (detector → responder) or the generic cross-plugin `DispatchCommand` RPC (detector → flow-source `show` commands), never a direct import across plugin boundaries.

## Flow
1. **Shared capture entry point.** Both `trafficusage` and `flow-export` declare `Dependencies: []string{"interface"}` in their registration so the interface plugin's rate tracker starts even if nothing else needs it (`trafficusage/register.go`, `flowexport/register.go`); both subscribe its ~1 Hz snapshot via `iface.SubscribeCollectNotify`. Both refuse to start as an external plugin process because that subscription is a same-process Go call with no cross-process fallback (`trafficusage/register.go`, `flowexport/register.go`).
2. **traffic-usage: attach/detach reconcile.** `Monitor.onSnapshot` (`trafficusage/monitor.go`) re-resolves every configured interface each tick and drives `reconcileLocked` (`trafficusage/monitor.go`), which attaches eBPF TCX programs to interfaces that are present/up/desired and detaches the rest (also on a `track-ip`/`max-entries` change, since those are baked into the loaded program).
3. **traffic-usage: poll + observation-feed publish.** A separate poller (`Monitor.poll`, `trafficusage/monitor.go`) reads the BPF maps every `cfg.Interval`; `publishLocked` (`trafficusage/monitor.go`) sets Prometheus series and, only for `track-ip` interfaces, publishes one `observation.Observation{Kind: KindSourceIP}` per source IP into `observation.Global()` (`trafficusage/monitor.go`), the tap the anomaly branch consumes. Egress byte totals stay in the interface `counts` snapshot, surfaced only via `show traffic-usage` (`trafficusage/show.go`, `egress-ips` at `trafficusage/show.go`), the DDoS branch's fast-target source (step 8).
4. **flow-export: conntrack dump + destroy events.** `conntrackWorker.run` (`flowexport/conntrack_worker.go`) dumps the kernel conntrack table every `active-timeout` seconds — OR on demand: a `refreshCh` signal (from `conntrackWorker.Refresh`, fired by the `AttackDetected` subscription so the DDoS characterizer sees an in-progress attack, not a stale ring) triggers an extra `dumpAndExport` on the same goroutine, coalesced so a burst of triggers cannot queue a backlog. `dumpAndExport` (`flowexport/conntrack_worker.go`) deltas each entry via the `conntrack.DeltaTracker` and calls `exporter.exportFlows` (`flowexport/exporter.go`). A parallel `runDestroy` listener (`flowexport/conntrack_worker.go`) exports short-lived flows the periodic dump would otherwise miss, tombstoning (not deleting) the delta baseline so a stale in-flight dump still computes a zero delta.
5. **exportFlows: BGP enrichment + recent-flow ring tap.** `exportFlows` (`flowexport/exporter.go`) applies BGP next-hop/AS enrichment when `enrichment.bgp` is configured, a `bgpEnrichBuilder` (`flowexport/enrichbgp.go`) subscribes RIB best-path-change events and rebuilds an atomically-swapped radix tree the `Enricher` (`flowexport/enrich/enricher.go`) reads lock-free, then taps every (enriched) flow into the bounded `recentRing` (`recentRing.append`, `flowexport/recent.go`) used by `show flow recent` (`flowexport/cmd_show.go`, render contract at `flowexport/cmd_show.go`). The ring exists only when `conntrack.Enabled` (`flowexport/exporter.go`) and is IPv4+IPv6 capable, unlike trafficusage's IPv4-only egress-ips map.
6. **exportFlows: collector fan-out + observation-feed publish.** The same call fans out NetFlow v9/IPFIX flow records to configured collectors and publishes one `observation.Observation{Kind: KindFlow}` per flow into `observation.Global()` (`flowexport/exporter.go`), the same feed trafficusage taps in step 3, fanning both plugins' facts into one place.
7. **Independent export side-paths (feed no detector).** `notifyFromRateTracker` (`flowexport/register.go`) converts the shared rate-tracker snapshot into a `CounterSnapshot` and calls `exporter.notifySnapshot` (`flowexport/exporter.go`), driving sFlow/NetFlow9/IPFIX interface-counter export. Separately, `samplingWorker.run` (`flowexport/sampling_worker.go`) reads kernel `psample` packets sampled by a `tc` sample action and calls `exporter.exportFlowSample` (`flowexport/exporter.go`) for sFlow flow-sample export. Both share the exporter but are orthogonal to DDoS/anomaly detection.
8. **Neutral facts layer: trafficstat.** `trafficstat.Service` lazily subscribes `observation.Global()` on first consumer attach (`trafficstat.EnsureGlobal`, `internal/component/trafficstat/register.go`) and is refcounted so an unconfigured detector costs nothing. `Service.start` (`internal/component/trafficstat/service.go`) ingests into a rolling aggregator and ticks every second, delivering `InterfaceEntry` rates to subscribers via `SubscribeRates` (`internal/component/trafficstat/service.go`), `ddos-detect`'s preferred rate source (step 9).
9. **Neutral facts layer: trafficfeature.** `trafficfeature.Service.start` (`internal/component/trafficfeature/service.go`, `EnsureGlobal` at `internal/component/trafficfeature/register.go`) ingests the SAME feed independently rather than deriving from `trafficstat.Snapshot`, fan-out and port-entropy need the raw 5-tuple stream, which trafficstat's lossy top-N snapshot cannot supply (learned 1046), producing per-source `FeatureEntry` vectors (fan-out, out/in ratio, port-entropy, new-peer, rare-port, beaconing). Neither neutral layer computes a verdict; that is the detectors' job below.
10. **ddos-detect: rate tick → threshold → state machine.** `runEngine`'s `subscribe` closure (`ddos/detect/register.go`) prefers `trafficstat.EnsureGlobal().SubscribeRates(d.onRates)`, falling back to raw `iface.SubscribeCollectNotify(d.onRate)` when trafficstat is unavailable (external plugin only warns, does not refuse, `ddos/detect/register.go`). Each tick (`detector.onRates`, `ddos/detect/detector.go`, or `onRate`, `ddos/detect/detector.go`) finds the max-RxPps interface and calls `applyTick` (`ddos/detect/detector.go`): feeds the rolling `baseline.Add` (`ddos/detect/baseline.go`, excluding attack/above-threshold samples so an ongoing flood cannot poison its own baseline), computes `threshold = max(p99*multiplier, floor)` (`ddos/detect/baseline.go`), and ticks `stateMachine.Tick` (`ddos/detect/state.go`: idle→confirming→active→clearing, gated by `confirm-duration`/`clear-consecutive-checks`).
11. **Trigger → fast signal off the hot path.** `stateMachine.activate` (`ddos/detect/state.go`) calls `detector.onAttackStart` (`ddos/detect/detector.go`), which snapshots interface/peak/threshold under `d.mu` and spawns `characterizeAndEmit` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) on its own goroutine (`ddos/detect/detector.go`) so the rate tick and mutex are never blocked by the cross-plugin round-trip. `characterizeTarget` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) dispatches `"show traffic usage name <iface>"` through the injected `p.DispatchCommand`, the SAME generic cross-plugin RPC dispatch used for any CLI command (`pkg/plugin/sdk/sdk_engine.go`, see `ai/digests/plugin-transport.md`), not a direct function call, and `parseTopDestination` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) picks the highest cumulative-egress-bytes IP as the victim /32 or /128. `emitDetected` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) emits `ddosevent.Detected` (`AttackDetected`, family generic-flood, severity graded by `ddosevent.GradeSeverity`) under `d.mu`, guarded by the `attackGen` counter against a stale/superseded emit.
12. **Stage-2 flow characterization.** `characterizeFromFlows` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) resolves the attack's flows via `awaitClassifiableFlows`, which POLLS `"show flow recent [dst <prefix>]"` (`queryRecentFlows`) within `characterize-timeout` until the ring yields a non-generic family — because the ring only refreshes at the conntrack dump cadence (`active-timeout`, default 60s), so at confirm it holds pre-attack state. The freshness comes from step 11's `emitDetected`: `flow-export` subscribes to `AttackDetected` and forces an immediate out-of-band conntrack dump (`flowexport/register.go` → `conntrackWorker.Refresh`), and the poll waits for it. A hard source absence returns immediately (no retry). It drops flows outside `characterize-window` (`filterByWindow`), derives the victim from the dominant destination when trafficusage gave none (`dominantDestination`, `ddos/detect/characterize.go`, this is how an IPv6-only victim, invisible to trafficusage, still gets resolved from the ring), and `classifyFlows` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) grades UDP/TCP/ICMP packet-share dominance, reflection source ports, and SYN half-open ratio into an `AttackFamily` plus the narrowest discriminating `VectorTuple` (proto/ports/TCP flags), ranked top sources, and Shannon source-entropy. `emitCharacterized` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) emits `ddosevent.Characterized`, generation-guarded like step 11. No reachable flow source ⇒ no emit at all; responders simply keep acting on the coarse `AttackDetected` (never worse than before).
13. **ddos-local: on-host nft drop.** Subscribes `Detected`/`Characterized`/`Cleared` (`ddos/local/register.go`). Both `onDetected` (`ddos/local/responder.go`) and `onCharacterized` (`ddos/local/responder.go`) call `applyMitigation` (`ddos/local/responder.go`): requires `response-level == enforce`, honors the event's `SuppressMitigation` flag (set by the detector's traffic policy) and picks the netfilter hook by `Direction` (`hookForDirection`, `ddos/local/responder.go`), builds an nft drop `Term` from the vector (`buildDropTerm`, `ddos/local/match.go`), and installs it via `firewall.RegisterTables`+`ApplyAll` (`ddos/local/responder.go`), rolling the registry back to empty on apply failure so it cannot claim a live mitigation the kernel does not have. `onCleared` (`ddos/local/responder.go`) removes the table; the clear signal is trustworthy only because nft drops happen after the kernel's NIC RX counter increments (nft-only limitation, doc-confirmed).
14. **ddos-flowspec: announce-on-characterize + leak-probe.** Subscribes the same three events (`ddos/flowspec/register.go`). `onCharacterized` (`ddos/flowspec/responder.go`) is the normal path, waits for characterization before ever announcing upstream (AC-8: announcing blinds the box, so the rule must be right first time). `onDetected` (`ddos/flowspec/responder.go`) only announces early on a `critical`-severity fast signal with `blackhole-fallback` enabled. `announce` (`ddos/flowspec/responder.go`) calls package-var `announceFunc`/`withdrawFunc` and starts a `probe` (`ddos/flowspec/probe.go`: hold-down → wait → probe-rate trickle → re-tighten-with-backoff-or-withdraw, `probe.Tick`, `ddos/flowspec/probe.go`).
15. **Observability + cloud reporting fan-out.** `ddos-observe`'s `store.open`/`store.finalize` (`ddos/observe/store.go`, `ddos/observe/store.go`, subscribed at `ddos/observe/register.go`) hold a bounded incident ring for `show ddos incidents`. `ddos-flowtriq`'s `client.openIncident` (`ddos/flowtriq/client.go`) reports the same `AttackDetected` to the Flowtriq cloud API. Both are independent event subscribers, not in the mitigation critical path.
16. **anomaly-detect: tick over trafficfeature.** `runEngine`'s `startTicker` (`anomaly/detect/register.go`) attaches to `trafficfeature.EnsureGlobal()` and ticks every second calling `detector.onTick` (`anomaly/detect/detector.go`), which builds per-cohort-prefix stats (`buildCohorts`, `anomaly/detect/detector.go`) and scores every tracked entity (`scoreEntity`, `anomaly/detect/detector.go`): continuous features (fan-out, out/in-ratio, port-entropy, beaconing) take `max(self zScore, cohort rarity)` (`anomaly/detect/score.go`, `anomaly/detect/score.go`); binary features (new-peer, rare-port) contribute exactly one threshold unit. `combineScore` (`anomaly/detect/score.go`) takes the strongest z-score at full weight plus a discounted sum of the rest, capped at 30, never a naive sum.
17. **Freeze-learn + confirm/clear.** Baseline updates fold into the entity's EWMA only when it is NOT anomalous this tick, or still inside `warmupTicks` (`onTick`, `anomaly/detect/detector.go`), so a sustained anomaly cannot drift its own baseline until it looks normal. Crossing `ConfirmDuration` consecutive above-threshold ticks calls `d.activate` (`anomaly/detect/detector.go`, emit at `anomaly/detect/detector.go`), which appends to a 128-entry recent-incident ring and emits `anomalyevent.Detected`; falling below `ClearConsecutive` emits `anomalyevent.Cleared` (`anomaly/detect/detector.go`, `anomaly/detect/detector.go`).
18. **anomaly-shape: shadow-first per-source arm.** Subscribes `Detected`/`Ongoing`/`Cleared` (`anomaly/shape/register.go`). `onDetected` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) checks kill-switch/shadow-mode/allowlist/blast-radius-cap, then arms a per-source firewall rate-limit (`reinstall`, whole-owner-table replace, `anomaly/shape/responder.go`). `onOngoing` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) extends the TTL for a still-anomalous entity.
19. **anomaly-shape: auto-revert + kill-switch.** `rearm` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) bumps a responder-level monotonic `gen` and binds a new timer to it; `autoRevertFire` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) withdraws only if the record's `gen` still matches, so a stale timer from a superseded arming is a no-op. `onCleared` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) withdraws early via `withdraw` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`); `killSwitch` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) reverts every armed rule and forces shadow mode, the single production path to that method (see gotchas).

## Invariants & gotchas
- **In-process is load-bearing, three different severities.** `trafficusage`/`flow-export` *refuse to start* as an external plugin process (`trafficusage/register.go`, `flowexport/register.go`) because `iface.SubscribeCollectNotify` is a same-process Go call with no cross-process fallback. `ddos-detect` only *warns* for the identical reason on both its rate-source paths (`ddos/detect/register.go`), an existing severity-framing inconsistency, not a bug, but worth knowing before debugging "detector never fires" on an external plugin.
- **Two independent lossy views of one feed, by design.** `trafficstat` and `trafficfeature` both subscribe `observation.Global()` directly rather than one deriving from the other's `Snapshot`, because fan-out/port-entropy need the raw per-flow tuple that trafficstat's lossy top-N snapshot cannot supply (learned 1046). Do not "simplify" one into a consumer of the other.
- **Characterization is cross-plugin RPC, not a function call.** `ddos/detect/characterize.go` resolves the victim and classifies flows by dispatching `"show traffic usage name <iface>"` and `"show flow recent"` through `p.DispatchCommand`, the same generic mechanism any CLI `show` command uses (`ai/digests/plugin-transport.md`). It degrades gracefully at every step (absent source → generic-flood with no target; absent flow-recent → keep the coarse target), so a missing `traffic-usage`/`flow-export` config never blocks detection, only narrowing.
- **`attackGen` fences every async emit.** `characterizeAndEmit` runs off the hot path; `emitDetected`/`emitCharacterized` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`,`:149`) re-check `d.attackGen == gen` under `d.mu` before emitting, so a `Cleared` racing a slow characterization query cannot leave `ddos-local` with a drop and no matching clear. `detector.Stop` sets `stopped` under `d.mu` before `wg.Wait` for the same reason, a late `onAttackStart` cannot add to the WaitGroup after `Wait` has started.
- **Exemption is a detector-side policy, not a per-responder allowlist.** The old `shouldMitigate`/`shouldAnnounce` allowlist checks are removed. The `ddos/detect` traffic policy (`ddos/detect/policy.go`: longest-prefix allow/deny rules) decides exempt-vs-mitigate once and encodes it on the event as `SuppressMitigation`; responders obey the flag (they cannot read the detect-owned policy). A detection-scope allow rule suppresses the event entirely.
- **`ddos-flowspec`'s upstream path is not wired to a real announcer.** `announceFunc`/`withdrawFunc` (`ddos/flowspec/responder.go`) are package-var stubs that only log `"cp-survival-4 not yet wired"`; `probeTick` (`ddos/flowspec/responder.go`) has no production caller (only `responder_test.go` invokes it directly). The responder's alert/enforce gating, SuppressMitigation/direction gating, and leak-probe state machine are all real and unit-tested, but today the plugin never actually announces or withdraws a BGP FlowSpec rule, nor observes leaked traffic, it only logs intent. Read this before trusting the doc's "a surgical BGP FlowSpec rule is announced" narrative at face value.
- **Poisoning guards appear in both branches, same shape.** `ddos/detect/baseline.go`'s `Add` excludes attack/above-threshold samples from the rolling p99; `anomaly/detect/detector.go`'s freeze-learn excludes anomalous/still-warming ticks from the EWMA fold. Both exist so a sustained attack/anomaly cannot raise its own detection bar.
- **Cohort rarity is leave-one-out and excludes +Inf-ratio members.** `cohortStats.rarity` (`anomaly/detect/score.go`) removes the scored entity's own contribution before computing the cohort mean/variance, and `buildCohorts` (`anomaly/detect/detector.go`) excludes an infinite out/in-ratio (pure exfil sender) from the cohort's ratio baseline entirely, otherwise the outlier dominates its own cohort statistics and masks milder peers (learned 1048).
- **`anomaly-shape` auto-revert generation MUST be responder-level.** `rearm` (`anomaly/shape/responder.go`) bumps a single responder-wide `gen` counter, not a per-record one; a per-record counter would reset to 1 on re-arm and let a stale timer from the FIRST arming match the new record's gen and wrongly withdraw a fresh mitigation (learned 1049, regression `TestStaleTimerAcrossReArmNoop`). Auto-revert fires regardless of any `Cleared` event, it is the safety ceiling, not a convenience.
- **`anomaly-shape`'s kill-switch has exactly one path.** `activate()` calls `resp.killSwitch()` when `cfg.KillSwitch` (`anomaly/shape/register.go`); an earlier cut set the `killed` flag directly in `newResponder` and relied on `Stop()`'s side effect, which left the `killSwitch()` method and its metric permanently unwired in production (learned 1049).
- **Local-mode clear depends on nft ordering; not portable to XDP.** `ddos-local`'s clear works because nft drops occur after the kernel NIC RX counter increments, so the detector's RxPps signal still reflects the (dropped) flood. An XDP_DROP backend would break this ordering; local mode is nft-only today.
- **flow-export's recent-ring and trafficusage's egress-ips have different blind spots.** The ring exists only when `conntrack.Enabled` (`flowexport/exporter.go`) but is IPv4+IPv6 capable; trafficusage's egress-ips map is IPv4-only but needs only `track-ip`. An IPv6-only victim is invisible to the fast target and is recovered solely via `dominantDestination` (`ddos/detect/characterize.go`) inside Stage-2 characterization.
- **Four doctor checks, all warnings not errors; three config-tree, one runtime probe.** `ddos/detect/doctor.go` (`checkFlowSource`), `anomaly/detect/doctor.go` (`checkFeatureSource`), and `anomaly/shape/doctor.go` (`checkFirewall`) read the config tree directly (they fire even if the dependency plugin would fail to attach for an unrelated reason). `flowexport/doctor.go` (`checkConntrackTracking`, `doctor-flowexport-conntrack-unavailable`) is the odd one out: it is config-gated (conntrack export enabled) but then PROBES THE KERNEL (`/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`) because conntrack export silently produces an empty recent-flow ring when nf_conntrack is not loaded/tracking -- and on gokrazy nothing but ze runs, so nothing else loads it. On the appliance ze now sets it up itself: `flowexport/conntrack_setup_appliance_linux.go` (`//go:build linux && ze_appliance`, called from `conntrackWorker.Start`) loads nf_conntrack/nf_conntrack_netlink, enables `nf_conntrack_acct`, and installs a minimal `ct`-referencing nftables rule via `google/nftables` (no `nft` binary on gokrazy) to register the tracking hooks netns-wide; off the appliance it is a no-op (`conntrack_setup_other.go`). All four warn, never block config apply.
- **Counter export and packet sampling are NOT part of the DDoS/anomaly data path.** `notifyFromRateTracker`/`exporter.notifySnapshot` (sFlow/NetFlow/IPFIX interface counters, step 7) and `samplingWorker` (per-packet sFlow samples, step 7) share the same `exporter` and rate-tracker callback as the conntrack path, but neither touches `observation.Global()` or any detector; only `exportFlows` (conntrack) does. Do not assume enabling sampling or counter collectors affects detection.
